subject.title: [Feature]: Compaction: configurable model override + flush-then-reset mode

question: Should OpenClaw add an opt-in mode that resets a session after a successful pre-compaction memory flush instead of running compaction, and should that decision be unified with the broader reset-time memory-flush policy?
rationale: Source inspection shows the remaining gap, but the behavior affects silent tool-capable execution, memory retention, provider/auth routing, user-visible session continuity, and config defaults, so automation should not choose the permanent policy.

options.title: Define one bounded reset-memory policy
options.body: Approve an opt-in reset-after-flush design that also aligns with the open pre-reset memory flush issue and specifies timeout, consent, audit, security, and fallback behavior.

options.title: Keep compaction as the recovery path
options.body: Reject automatic reset after successful flush and rely on compaction plus the existing model overrides for cost control.

options.title: Move the remaining work to the reset issue
options.body: Narrow this issue to the model overrides already shipped and make https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/45608 the canonical reset-lifecycle design thread.

recommendation.title: Define one bounded reset-memory policy
recommendation.body: Approve an opt-in reset-after-flush design that also aligns with the open pre-reset memory flush issue and specifies timeout, consent, audit, security, and fallback behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete is tied to both the memory-flush primitive and the reset/session paths implicated by the remaining product decision.
